content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem with the key facts: the monthly-spend-feature flag went live at 23:28, a divide-by-zero in spend_summary.py:35 caused roughly 30% of account page requests to fail, and the 23:33:24 rollback attempt didn't take effect since logs still show the flag on. I need to avoid stating any impact figures myself since I'm not being asked to compute the incident cost.

I'll keep the impact description qualitative rather than numeric, note that the outage duration is a lower bound since the service hadn't recovered at the last metric read, and flag that the flag-revert failure is inferred from logs rather than confirmed with the flag provider. I'll also note the change-event lookback returned inconsistent counts across overlapping windows, making the change record unreliable, and I'll keep the executive summary generic — describing "customer account pages" and "a newly switched-on feature" rather than naming components directly.

assumptions: The feature-flag revert is assumed to have failed to propagate rather than to have been re-enabled; this is inferred from the service's flag-evaluation log lines continuing to read 'on' after both off-toggles, and was not confirmed against the flag provider's own state.
The crash is assumed to affect only the account-page render path, because that is the only request type appearing in the error logs read; no other endpoints were sampled.

The impact window is assumed to begin at 23:28 (first minute with the new error and with the flag evaluating 'on') and to extend past the last metric read; the end of the outage is unknown, so all impact is a lower bound.

The change-event lookups returned inconsistent counts for overlapping windows (0, then 2, then 3, then 0 production changes), so the conclusion that no deploy preceded the incident rests on an unreliable change record.
The pre-incident error floor is assumed to be unrelated background noise: those failures are client disconnects, a different error class from the division-by-zero seen after 23:28.
The proposed draft pull request is assumed to be unverified; nothing in this record shows it was reviewed, merged, or tested against the failure.
input.executive_summary: Starting at 23:28 UTC on 22 September 2026, a large share of customers loading their account page on the online shop got an error instead of the page. The cause was a newly switched-on feature that computes a monthly spend summary; the code behind it crashes on certain accounts. Automated monitoring raised the alert about five minutes later and the automated responder tried to switch the feature back off, but the shop's own logs show the feature still running afterwards, so the switch-off did not take hold and customers kept seeing errors. The service had not recovered by the last minute of data available, so the outage lasted at least from 23:28 onward — the true end time is not known from this record. Because no automated action could resolve it, the incident was escalated to engineers with a draft code change proposed to fix the crash. Only the account page was affected; browsing and the rest of the shop were not implicated by the evidence reviewed.
input.root_cause: The `monthly-spend-feature` flag flipped from off to on at 23:28 on io-shop, and the code path it gates raises an unguarded ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:35, so every account-page render that took the new path failed; the error appears in the first minute the flag evaluated "on" and no deploy or config change is recorded in any lookback window. Argus's flag revert at 23:33:24 did not restore service — the service's own logs kept reporting `monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations` at 23:34–23:37 — so the off-toggle appears never to have reached the evaluating instances, and the incident remained open and was escalated with a draft pull request to guard the division.
